OpenTempl is a free design app for posters, social posts and slides. It runs in the browser and as a desktop app, needs no account, and keeps what you make on your own computer. The code is open source under the MIT license.

## What is in 0.1.0

- 337 templates in 34 styles, including 12 full presentation decks. Every part of a template can be changed.
- A Start page where you describe what you are making and pick a size: poster, story, post, slides, A4 or custom.
- Generate: write a few words and get a design in one of the styles. Use your own OpenAI key, or use it free through your ChatGPT account.
- Unsplash photos, searched from inside the editor.
- Live sharing with end to end encrypted sync, so you can edit the same design with someone else.
- Import PDF and PowerPoint files and keep working on them.
- Export to the formats you are likely to need, including PNG, PDF, PowerPoint, GIF and MP4.
- Works offline. Designs are saved on your machine.

## Installing

The builds are not code signed yet, so your system will ask before it opens them the first time.

- macOS: open the dmg and drag OpenTempl to Applications. If macOS says the app cannot be opened, right click it, choose Open, and confirm. Or go to System Settings, Privacy and Security, and choose Open Anyway.
- Windows: run the installer. If SmartScreen shows a warning, choose More info, then Run anyway.
- Linux: make the AppImage executable and run it, or install the deb package.

Pick the arm64 dmg for Apple silicon Macs and the x64 dmg for Intel Macs. The SHA256SUMS.txt file lists a checksum for every download.

Try it without installing anything at https://opentempl.org
